subject: Service provider designation and dataflow mapping for US state privacy addendum
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procure Team <procure-acme@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify role and dataflow for US state privacy addendum

Kimberly —

Thanks for sending the draft US state privacy addendum. A couple of quick asks from legal and procurement so we can move to internal review:

- Can you confirm Redwood's exact designation under CCPA/CPRA and state statutes (service provider vs. processor)? Our legal needs explicit language plus an example of how subprocessors are handled (notice cadence and approval threshold).
- We also need a high-level dataflow map showing what fields are sent to Redwood, where (regions) they’re processed, and any onward transfers to subprocessors.

Can you attach a short mapping and your current subprocessor list? Procurement is on a 12/20 cadence and we’re trying to get this into the queue.

Appreciate it —
Dana
Dana Li
Sr. Contracts Manager
Acme Health
attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify role and dataflow for US state privacy addendum

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:
- Redwood accepts the "service provider" / "designated service provider" characterization under CCPA/CPRA and equivalent state addenda. We will not use the data for our own purposes beyond providing the service.
- Subprocessors: we have an established subprocessors list and a 30-day notice process for material additions; for anything critical (e.g., new cloud regions or analytics providers) we can add an approval step in the addendum.

I’m attaching a concise dataflow map and our current subprocessor summary. Marcus and Laura are looped for any legal/contract-level notes before I send back to your team.

Next steps: if your legal is okay with the service-provider language and the 30-day notice + granular exceptions for critical subprocessors, we can issue a DocuSign-ready addendum by EOD 12/18.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
attachments: redwood_uspa_data_flow_map.xlsx; Acme_DPA_Proposed_2026-12-15.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:21:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: review of service provider wording & subprocessor notice

Kim —

Quick internal note before we finalize:
- Confirmed: designate as "Service Provider" with the limited-use clause (no repurposing of personal data). That aligns with our hosted + dedicated offerings.
- Data residency: for Acme we should offer the ability to pin processing to a US region; the dataflow map should call out token-level telemetry that may be collected for billing/ops and how it is pseudonymized.
- Subprocessor cadence: 30-day notice is standard; for new infra subprocessors (e.g., new cloud region or managed GPU provider) ask for prior notice and an escalation route to security team — optional approval for enterprise customers.

Also flagged a single redline in the addendum: they requested an overly broad right to audit subprocessors; suggest we limit to annual audits with SOC2 reports or a security questionnaire + onsite only by exception. Laura, your take?

- Marcus
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: review of service provider wording & subprocessor notice

Agree with Marcus. A couple of concrete edits to propose back to Acme:

1) Service provider language: keep the "limited use" paragraph and add a short illustrative example of permitted processing (hosting, inference, logging for diagnosis) vs. prohibited repurposing (training new models on customer data).

2) Subprocessor visibility: provide the current list in the addendum and commit to 30-day notice + an option for Acme to request advance notice for"critical" subprocessors. Define critical = any subprocessor with access to unredacted PHI or infra hosting across regions.

3) Audit scope: offer SOC2 + security questionnaire as default proof; allow onsite or third-party audit with mutually agreeable scope and cost allocation.

I can draft the redlines and return to Kimberly for signature.

- Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procure Team <procure-acme@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Final: US state addendum — service provider designation + dataflow map attached

Dana —

Thanks again for the patience. Attached are two files: a) a redlined addendum that preserves the "service provider" / "limited use" language and includes the proposed subprocessor notice + critical-subprocessor carveout, and b) a one-page dataflow map that lists the fields we receive, processing region (US-west), and subprocessors that may receive pseudonymized telemetry.

Key points for Acme:
- Redwood will be designated as a Service Provider under CCPA/CPRA and relevant state addenda; the addendum includes explicit limited-use restrictions and an example clause on prohibited uses (e.g., model training).
- Subprocessors: current list included; 30-day notice for new subprocessors, with prior notice and escalation for critical infra/providers.
- Audit: SOC2 reports and a security questionnaire will be provided; onsite audits are by exception with cost allocation.

Next step: if this aligns with Acme Legal, we will convert the redline to a DocuSign addendum and circulate for signature. DocuSign link (preview) is included here: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?tf=01abcdef...

Attachments: redwood_uspa_data_flow_map.xlsx; Acme_DPA_Proposed_2026-12-15.pdf

Would you like us to proceed to DocuSign by EOD PST?

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
